# Monthly totals changed after upgrading to 2.4.0

Opened by: Hanna Lindqvist (finance operations)
Label: bug

We upgraded tally from 2.3.0 to 2.4.0 last week. Since then the March report for our ledger no
longer agrees with our books. We ran the same command with both releases on the same file
(attached as `ledger.csv`), from a checkout of each release tag:

    python -m tally report --month 2026-03 ledger.csv

With 2.3.0:

    Totals for 2026-03
    FACILITIES      9737797.03
    OPS-EAST        9797853.14
    OPS-WEST        9520134.15
    R-AND-D         9845592.45
    SALES-EU        9357861.70
    SALES-NA        9822616.26
    SUPPORT         9357144.38
    TRAVEL          9621229.77
    TOTAL          77060228.88

With 2.4.0:

    Totals for 2026-03
    FACILITIES    9,733,101.94
    OPS-EAST      9,810,599.90
    OPS-WEST      9,506,813.45
    R-AND-D       9,843,916.57
    SALES-EU      9,348,230.47
    SALES-NA      9,839,299.40
    SUPPORT       9,345,391.04
    TRAVEL        9,622,364.07
    TOTAL        77,049,716.84

The 2.3.0 figures are the ones our accountants signed off. Nothing changed on our side: same file,
same command, same machine. We did not try the releases in between.

steps.message:
The regression came in with commit `9a04783d6814f5ec0fd63dc91f0e3035a88c2189`, "Share timestamp parsing between readers and exports". The file that causes it is `tally/dates.py`, and the earliest tag containing the commit is `v2.4.0rc1`. I wrote the answer to `/app/answer.json` and `/app/STATUS.json`.

I ran `python -m tally report --month 2026-03` on the reported ledger at every commit between v2.3.0 and v2.4.0, and compared the figures with the report's two sets of totals. The result was 112 commits in a row that were good or gave other totals, then 59 bad ones from this commit on.

The parent commit gives the 2.3.0 totals and this one gives the 2.4.0 totals. The change to `tally/dates.py` makes `parse_stamp` convert every timestamp to UTC. Rows with a time zone offset can then land on a different day, and so in a different month. The commit also touched `tally/io/readers.py` and `tally/report.py`, but those two changes only reword code and rename a variable.

I did not test reverting `tally/dates.py` on its own to confirm the totals return to 2.3.0. The attribution rests on reading the diff.
